c.tagline: Saharan palm oasis of brick medinas, salt lakes, and Star Wars sands.

taxi.fareNote: Yellow taxis are metered and cheap; shared 'louages' (fixed-route minibuses) link Tozeur with Nefta, Kebili and other towns, and horse-drawn 'calèches' run tourist loops through the oasis. No ride-hailing apps operate.

emergency.note: 197 reaches the police and 190 the ambulance/SAMU; 198 is the civil-protection/fire service.

avoid.reason: Southern desert — remote areas near the Algeria/Libya borders are restricted; check advisories

hood_desc: Tozeur's 14th-century medina, a warren of alleys built from ochre bricks laid in raised geometric patterns unique to the Jerid; small guesthouses, craft shops and museums make it the atmospheric historic base.
The modern spine of town along the main avenue, with cafes, banks, the covered market and the louage/bus stations; the practical, central place to sort logistics and eat.

A landscaped strip of resort hotels, spas and pools running toward the oasis and the Dar Cheraït museum and Chak Wak heritage park; best for travelers wanting a full-service base with a pool after desert days.
The old oasis settlement at the palm grove's heart, with the Belvédère rocks, an ancient mosque and traditional farming hamlets; a calm, local counterpoint to the tourist strip.

water.note: Drink bottled water; tap water is not reliable for visitors.

transit.hours: Taxis run through the day and evening; louages depart when full, mostly in daylight.
transit.note: Tozeur has no urban bus network; the town is small and flat, so most trips are on foot, by cheap metered taxi, or by calèche or bicycle through the oasis.
transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash (dinars) to the driver; taxis are metered and louages charge a fixed per-seat rate.

bus: SNTRI intercity coaches to Tunis (~7 hr), Kairouan and Gafsa
Louages (shared minibuses) to Nefta, Kebili, Gafsa and Douz
train: No passenger rail to Tozeur; nearest railhead is Metlaoui/Gafsa (the Lézard Rouge tourist train runs from Metlaoui)

transit.m: Metered taxi to the city centre (~5-10 min)

tip.r: ~10% at restaurants; round up for taxis and tip guides and hotel staff a dinar or two.

food.name: Couscous bel allouch (lamb couscous)
food.desc: Steamed semolina piled with slow-cooked lamb, chickpeas and oasis vegetables in a red harissa-spiked broth; the Friday dish of southern Tunisia.

places.name: Restaurant Le Petit Prince
places.area: Palm grove, off Avenue Abou el Kacem Chebbi
places.note: Long-running garden restaurant in the oasis; the standard address for a full couscous lunch

places.name: Restaurant El Firma

places.name: Diar Abou Habibi
places.note: Palm-frond eco-lodge serving set-menu couscous with vegetables grown on site

food.name: Brik a l'oeuf
food.desc: Paper-thin malsouka pastry folded around a whole egg with tuna, parsley and capers, then fried so the yolk still runs when you bite in.

places.name: Restaurant Le Soleil
places.note: Central old-school restaurant; brik arrives blistering hot as a starter before the grills

places.name: Dar Deda
places.note: Guesthouse dining room in the brick-patterned old town, known for homestyle brik variations

places.name: Snack stalls on Avenue Habib Bourguiba
places.note: Evening fricasse-and-brik counters where locals eat; cheapest and freshest version in town

food.name: Mtabga (Berber pizza)
food.desc: Semolina flatbread stuffed with spiced lamb or vegetables, onion and tomato, baked or griddled and cut in wedges - the desert answer to pizza.

places.name: Ksar Rouge
places.note: Red-brick restaurant complex with a bread oven turning out mtabga and tajines

places.name: Restaurant El Firma
places.note: Reliable rolled Berber pizza, spicy version on request

places.name: Marche Central de Tozeur
places.note: Market bakers sell mtabga and mlawi wraps hot from the plate through the morning

food.name: Deglet Nour dates
food.desc: Tozeur's translucent honey-coloured date, the finger of light, eaten fresh off the branch or stuffed with almond paste as a sweet.

places.name: Eden Palm
places.note: Working date farm and museum with tastings, date syrup and stuffed dates to take away

places.name: Marche Central de Tozeur
places.note: Stalls sell branch dates by weight; ask for this season's harvest, not vacuum packs

places.name: Date shops on Avenue Habib Bourguiba
places.note: Cluster of family cooperatives selling graded Deglet Nour and date paste

food.name: Makroud
food.desc: Diamond-cut semolina pastry packed with date paste, fried and dunked in honey - the classic Tozeur sweet, best eaten the day it is made.

places.name: Patisseries on Avenue Habib Bourguiba
places.note: Trays of fresh makroud and ghriba sold by the piece all afternoon

places.name: Eden Palm
places.note: Date-based pastries made on site, useful if you want them boxed for the road

places.name: Dar Deda
places.note: Homemade makroud served with mint tea at the end of the set menu

food.name: Grilled camel and merguez
food.desc: Desert-country grill: skewers of camel or slow-cooked camel tajine alongside fiery lamb merguez sausage, served with harissa and flatbread.

places.name: Ksar Rouge
places.note: Camel dishes are a house speciality, cooked long so the meat stays moist

places.name: Restaurant Le Petit Prince
places.note: Mixed grills with merguez under the palms; order ahead for camel

places.name: Grill stalls at Marche Central
places.note: Butchers grill merguez to order at lunchtime, eaten in bread on the spot

food.name: Mint tea with pine nuts
food.desc: Sweet green tea poured from a height over a handful of toasted pine nuts or almonds; the standard welcome in every Tozeur cafe and courtyard.

places.name: Cafes in the Ouled El Hadef medina
places.note: Shaded courtyards among the patterned brickwork, cheapest and most local pour

places.name: Dar Cherait complex
places.note: Museum cafe with terrace seating and the full pine-nut tea ritual

places.name: Eden Palm
places.note: Tea served after the date-farm tour, often with a date pastry

food.name: Lagmi (palm sap)
food.desc: Milky sap tapped from the crown of a date palm at dawn, drunk fresh and sweet the same morning; a traditional oasis drink that ferments fast.

places.name: Eden Palm
places.note: Explains and offers the tapping tradition; the easiest place for visitors to try it

landmarks: Ouled el-Hadef Medina
Tozeur's 14th-century old quarter mesmerises with geometric patterns of protruding ochre bricks, a unique decorative style adorning every wall of its shaded alleys.
Palmeraie of Tozeur
Over 400,000 date palms fed by ancient springs form one of the Sahara's greatest oases, best explored by calèche among gardens producing prized deglet nour dates.
Dar Chraiet Museum
A lavish private museum in a palatial setting displays Tunisian costumes, jewellery and period rooms recreating the refined domestic life of old Tozeur.
Belvédère Rocks
At the palmeraie's edge, these sculpted sandstone outcrops overlook springs and palm tops, a favourite sunset perch above the oasis with distant Chott views.
Chak Wak Park
An eccentric theme park beside the palmeraie narrates Earth's history from dinosaurs to the great faiths through gardens, dioramas and life-size sculptures.
Zoo du Sahara et Jardin du Paradis
A shaded botanical garden and small desert zoo set among the palm groves, where paths wind past bougainvillea and banana trees to enclosures of fennec foxes and horned vipers.
El Ferdous Mosque
A neighborhood mosque whose facade is laid in Tozeur's signature ochre brickwork, arranged in geometric relief patterns found only in this and nearby oasis towns.
Great Mosque of Tozeur
The city's oldest mosque, dating to around 1030, topped by a tall minaret and faced with the same yellow-brown brick patterning found across the old medina.
Central Market of Tozeur
A noisy, crowded covered market in the medina where stallholders sell dates, spices, fresh produce, and traditional pottery to a constant soundtrack of bargaining.
Sidi Abid Mosque
One of Tozeur's historic brick mosques, its patterned ochre facade ranking among the finest surviving examples of the town's traditional relief masonry technique.

train.note: No passenger rail reaches Tozeur; the nearest line is at Metlaoui/Gafsa, where the historic Lézard Rouge tourist train runs into the Seldja Gorge.

bus.note: SNTRI runs long-distance coaches to Tunis (~7 hr) via Gafsa and Kairouan; shared louages cover regional hops to Nefta, Kebili, Douz and Gafsa.

ferry.note: Tozeur lies deep in the southwestern desert beside the Chott el Jerid salt flat, which is dry for most of the year and has never been navigable, so there is no boat service of any kind. The nearest passenger sailings are the international ferries from La Goulette in Tunis, roughly 450 km northeast.

full.blurb: The mountain oases of the Jebel en-Negueb — waterfalls, palm gorges and abandoned villages, a classic full-day 4x4 loop.
full.name: Chebika, Tamerza & Mides

full.blurb: 'Gateway to the Sahara' with camel treks and the great erg dunes, about 2 hours southeast.
full.name: Douz

half.blurb: Vast shimmering salt lake crossed by the Tozeur-Kebili causeway, famous for mirages and pink-tinged crusts at sunrise.
half.name: Chott el-Djerid

half.blurb: Neighbouring oasis town with the Corbeille palm-filled crater and Sufi shrines, 25 km west.
half.name: Nefta

half.blurb: The preserved Star Wars film set of Anakin's home town, standing in the dunes toward Ong Jmel.
half.name: Mos Espa
Chebika Mountain Oasis
half.blurb: A spring-fed palm ravine cascades below the ruined old village at this cinematic corner of the Atlas foothills, gleaming golden against bare crags.

half.name: Tamerza Canyon and Cascades
half.blurb: Tunisia's grandest mountain oasis pairs a palm-lined canyon and waterfalls with an abandoned earthen village overlooking the gorge from its rocky perch.

half.name: Midès Gorge
half.blurb: This vertiginous canyon, its striped rock walls coiling round an ancient village near the Algerian border, starred in The English Patient and stuns photographers.
